<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">BUSINESS</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Forward Looking Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This Annual Report contains certain &#8220;forward-looking statements&#8221; which may be identified by the use of words such as &#8220;believe,&#8221; &#8220;expect,&#8221; &#8220;anticipate,&#8221; &#8220;should,&#8221; &#8220;planned,&#8221; &#8220;estimated&#8221; and &#8220;potential.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Examples of forward-looking statements include, but are not limited to, estimates with respect to the Company&#8217;s financial condition, results of operations and business that are subject to various factors which could cause actual results to differ materially from these estimates and most other statements that are not historical in nature.&#160;&#160;These factors include, but are not limited to, general and local economic conditions, changes in interest rates, deposit flows, demand for mortgage, commercial and other loans, real estate values, competition, changes in accounting principles, policies, or guidelines, changes in legislation or regulation, and other economic, competitive, governmental, regulatory, and technological factors affecting operations, pricing products and services.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Flatbush Federal Bancorp, Inc.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Flatbush Federal Bancorp, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a Federal corporation which was organized in 2003 as part of the mutual holding company reorganization of Flatbush Federal Savings &amp; Loan Association (the &#8220;Association&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s principal asset is its investment in Flatbush Federal Savings &amp; Loan Association.&#160;&#160;The Company is a majority owned subsidiary of Flatbush Federal Bancorp, MHC (&#8220;Flatbush MHC&#8221;), a Federally-chartered mutual holding company.&#160;&#160;Flatbush MHC owned 1,484,208 shares of common stock, or 54.23% of the outstanding shares of the common stock at December 31, 2010. At December 31, 2010, the Company had consolidated assets of $147.0 million, deposits of $117.1 million and stockholders&#8217; equity of $15.8 million.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s executive office is located at 2146 Nostrand Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11210 and its telephone number is (718) 859-6800.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Flatbush Federal Savings &amp; Loan Association</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>The Association&#8217;s principal business consists of attracting retail deposits from the general public in the areas surrounding its three locations in Brooklyn, New York and investing those deposits, together with funds generated from operations, primarily in one- to four-family residential mortgage loans, commercial real estate loans, construction loans, investment securities, and mortgage-backed securities.&#160;&#160;The Association&#8217;s revenues are derived principally from the interest on loans and securities, loan origination and servicing fees, bank owned life insurance (&#8220;BOLI&#8221;) income, and service charges and fees collected on deposit accounts.&#160;&#160;The Association&#8217;s primary sources of funds are deposits, principal and interest payments on loans and securities, and borrowings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>The Association faces intense competition within its market area both in making loans and attracting deposits.&#160;&#160;The New York City area has a high concentration of financial institutions including large money center and regional banks, community banks and credit unions.&#160;&#160;Some of the Association&#8217;s competitors offer products and services that it currently does not offer, such as trust services and private banking.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Association&#8217;s market share of deposits represented less than one half of one percent of deposits in Kings County.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Association&#8217;s competition for loans and deposits comes principally from commercial banks, savings institutions, mortgage banking firms and credit unions.&#160;&#160;The Association faces additional competition for deposits from short-term money market funds, brokerage firms, mutual funds and</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div id="FTR">

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">insurance companies.&#160;&#160;The primary focus is to build and develop profitable customer relationships across all lines of business while maintaining a role as a community bank.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Market Area.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>The Association operates in an urban market area that has a stable population and household base.&#160;&#160;The Association&#8217;s primary lending area is concentrated in Brooklyn, as well as the other four boroughs of New York City, and Long Island, New York.&#160;&#160;One- to four-family residential real estate in the market area is characterized by a large number of attached and semi-detached houses, including a number of two- and three-family homes and condominium apartments.&#160;&#160;Most of the deposit customers are residents of the greater New York metropolitan area.&#160;&#160;The economy of the market area is characterized by a large number of small retail establishments.&#160;&#160;The Association&#8217;s customer base is comprised of middle-income households, and to a lesser extent, low-to-moderate-income households.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Lending Activities.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Historically, the Association&#8217;s principal lending activity has been the origination of first mortgage loans for the purchase or refinancing of one- to four-family residential real property as well as multi-family and commercial real estate loans.&#160;&#160;Historically, the Association retained all loans that it originated.&#160;&#160;However, beginning in 2002 the Association sold a limited number of its one- to four-family loans, on a servicing retained basis, to the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York.&#160;&#160;No loans were sold during the year ended December 31, 2010.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>One- to four-family residential real estate mortgage loans represented $71.8 million, or 65.84%, of our loan portfolio at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The Association also offers commercial real estate loans, multifamily loans, condominium loans and construction loans secured by real estate. Construction loans totaled $7.8 million, or 7.14% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2010. Commercial real estate loans totaled $23.0 million, or 21.06% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans totaled $5.9 million, or 5.40% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;On a limited basis, non-real estate secured loans are originated and consist of passbook loans and credit card loans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The total amount of loans due after December 31, 2011 that have fixed interest rates is $74.5 million, and the total amount of loans due after such date which have floating or adjustable interest rates is $24.2 million. Of the $21.2 million of commercial real estate loans due after December 31, 2011, 12.43% have fixed interest rates and 87.57% have adjustable interest rates.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, there were no construction loans due after December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">One- to Four-Family Residential Loans.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>The Association&#8217;s lending activity includes the origination of one- to four-family residential mortgage loans that are primarily secured by properties located in Brooklyn, as well as the other four boroughs of New York City, and Long Island, New York.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, approximately $71.8 million, or 65.84% of our loan portfolio, consisted of one- to- four-family residential loans.&#160;&#160;Generally, one- to four-family residential mortgage loans are originated in amounts up to 80% of the lesser of the appraised value or purchase price of the property. Private mortgage insurance is required on loans with a loan-to-value ratio in excess of 80%.&#160;&#160;The Association will not make loans with a loan-to-value ratio in excess of 95% for loans secured by single family homes and 90% for loans secured by two- to four-family properties.&#160;&#160;Fixed-rate loans are originated for terms of 15 and 30 years.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the Association&#8217;s largest loan secured by one- to four-family real estate had a principal balance of $927,000 and was secured by a one-family residence.&#160;&#160;This loan was performing in accordance with its terms.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Association also offers adjustable-rate mortgage loans with one, two, three and five year adjustment periods based on changes in a designated United States Treasury index.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2010, the Association originated one adjustable rate mortgage for $200,000. In general, the adjustable rate mortgage loans provide for maximum rate adjustments of 200 basis points per adjustment, with a lifetime maximum adjustment of 600 basis points. Adjustable rate mortgage loans amortize over terms of up to 30 years.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Adjustable rate mortgage loans decrease the risk associated with changes in market interest rates by periodically repricing, but involve other risks because, as interest rates increase, the underlying payments by the borrower increase, thus increasing the potential for default by the borrower.&#160;&#160;At the same time, the marketability of the underlying collateral may be adversely affected by higher interest rates.&#160;&#160;Upward adjustment of the contractual interest rate is also limited by the maximum periodic and lifetime interest rate adjustments permitted by the loan documents, and therefore, is potentially limited in effectiveness during periods of rapidly rising interest rates.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, $3.4 million, or 4.7% of the Association&#8217;s one- to four-family residential loans had adjustable rates of interest.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All one- to four-family residential mortgage loans that the Association originates include &#8220;due-on-sale&#8221; clauses, which give the Association the right to declare a loan immediately due and payable in the event that, among other things, the borrower sells or otherwise disposes of the real property subject to the mortgage and the loan is not repaid.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulations limit the amount that a savings association may lend relative to the appraised value of the real estate securing the loan, as determined by an appraisal of the property at the time the loan is originated.&#160;&#160;For all loans, the Association utilizes outside independent appraisers approved by the board of directors.&#160;&#160;All borrowers are required to obtain title insurance.&#160;&#160;The Association also requires homeowner&#8217;s insurance and fire and casualty insurance and, where circumstances warrant, flood insurance on properties securing real estate loans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Multi-Family Real Estate Loans.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Loans secured by multi-family real estate totaled approximately $5.9 million, or 5.40% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans generally are secured by rental properties.&#160;&#160;Substantially all multi-family real estate loans are secured by properties located within the Association&#8217;s lending area.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Association had sixteen multi-family loans with an average principal balance of $368,000, and the largest multi-family real estate loan had a principal balance of $828,000.&#160;&#160;All of the loans secured by multi-family real estate properties are performing in accordance with their terms. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Multi-family real estate loans generally are offered with adjustable interest rates that adjust after five years.&#160;&#160;Multi-family loans are originated for terms of up to 15 years.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loan adjustments are tied to the prime rate as reported in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">The Wall Street Journal, </font>or the FHLB five year advance rate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Association considers a number of factors in originating multi-family real estate loans.&#160;&#160;Management evaluates the qualifications and financial condition of the borrower (including credit history), profitability and expertise, as well as the value and condition of the mortgaged property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;When evaluating the qualifications of the borrower, management considers the financial resources of the borrower, the borrower&#8217;s experience in owning or managing similar property and the borrower&#8217;s payment history with the Association and other financial institutions.&#160;&#160;In evaluating the property securing the loan, the factors considered include the net operating income of the mortgaged property before debt service and depreciation, the debt service coverage ratio (the ratio of net operating income to debt service) to ensure that it is at least 125% of the debt service, and the ratio of the loan amount to the appraised value of the mortgaged property.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans are originated in amounts up to 75% of the appraised value of the mortgaged property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;All multi-family loans are appraised by outside independent appraisers approved by the board of directors. An environmental inspection, performed by an independent environmental engineer approved by the board of directors, may be required on certain loans.&#160;&#160;Personal guarantees may be obtained from multi-family real estate borrowers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans secured by multi-family real estate generally involve a greater degree of credit risk than one- to four-family residential mortgage loans and carry larger loan balances.&#160;&#160;This increased credit risk is a result of several factors, including the concentration of principal in a limited number of loans and borrowers, the effects of general economic conditions on income producing properties, and the increased difficulty of evaluating and monitoring these types of loans.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, the repayment of loans secured by multi-family real estate typically depends upon the successful operation of the real estate property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;If the cash flow from the project is reduced, the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan may be impaired.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commercial Real Estate Loans.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>At December 31, 2010, $23.0 million, or 21.06% of the total loan portfolio consisted of commercial real estate loans.&#160;&#160;Commercial real estate loans are secured by office buildings, mixed use properties and other commercial properties.&#160;&#160;The Association generally originates adjustable rate commercial real estate loans, as well as balloon maturity loans, with maximum terms of up to 15 years.&#160;&#160;The maximum loan-to-value ratio of commercial real estate loans is 75%.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the Association had 43 commercial real estate loans with an average outstanding balance of $534,000.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the Association&#8217;s largest loan secured by commercial real estate was a $1.9 million loan. At December 31, 2010, this loan was performing in accordance with its terms.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, four loans totaling $2.6 million, secured by commercial real estate were not performing in accordance their terms.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Association considers a number of factors in originating commercial real estate loans.&#160;&#160;Management evaluates the qualifications and financial condition of the borrower (including credit history), profitability and expertise, as well as the value and condition of the mortgaged property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;When evaluating the qualifications of the borrower, management considers the financial resources of the borrower, the borrower&#8217;s experience in owning or managing similar property and the borrower&#8217;s payment history with the Association and other financial institutions.&#160;&#160;In evaluating the property securing the loan, the factors management considered include the net operating income of the mortgaged property before debt service and depreciation, the debt service coverage ratio (the ratio of net</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">operating income to debt service) to ensure that it is at least 125% of the debt service, and the ratio of the loan amount to the appraised value of the mortgaged property.&#160;&#160;&#160;All commercial real estate loans are appraised by outside independent appraisers approved by the board of directors. An environmental inspection is performed by an independent environmental engineer approved by the board of directors.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Personal guarantees may be obtained from commercial real estate borrowers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans secured by commercial real estate generally are larger than one- to four-family residential loans and involve greater credit risk.&#160;&#160;Commercial real estate loans often involve large loan balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers.&#160;&#160;Repayment of these loans depends to a large degree on the results of operations and management of the properties securing the loans or the businesses conducted on such property, and may be affected to a greater extent by adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy in general.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Construction Loans</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.&#160;&#160;</font>At December 31, 2010, $7.8 million, or 7.14% of the Association&#8217;s total loan portfolio consisted of construction loans.&#160;&#160;Construction loans are originated by the Association which currently offers adjustable-rate multi-family construction loans.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>The Association also participates in construction loans with adjustable rates for the construction of multifamily and non-residential real estate.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the largest construction loan was a $1.5 million participation of which $1.5 was advanced.&#160;&#160;The loan was non-performing and has a $497,000 specific valuation allowance.&#160;&#160;Construction loans have interest rates that adjust monthly and require the payment of interest only during the construction period.&#160;&#160;Construction loans will generally be made in amounts of up to 75% of the lower of the appraisal value of the property, or the actual cost of the improvements.&#160;&#160;Funds are disbursed in accordance with a schedule reflecting the completion of portions of the project.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the Association&#8217;s construction loans are secured by properties located in Brooklyn, Queens, Long Island and Manhattan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Construction loans generally involve a greater degree of credit risk than one- to four-family residential mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;The risk of loss on a construction loan depends upon the accuracy of the initial estimate of the value of the property at completion of construction compared to the estimated cost of construction.&#160;&#160;If the estimated cost of construction is inaccurate, funds may have to be advanced beyond the original amount committed in order to protect the value of the property. An environmental inspection is performed by an independent environmental engineer.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, because construction loans primarily consist of participation loans, the Company relies on other parties to document the loans. As a result, the Company has less control over the initial underwriting and monitoring of these loans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Loans</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.&#160;&#160;</font>The Association offers a variety of loans secured by real estate, or by property other than real estate.&#160;&#160;These loans include loans secured by deposits, home equity loans, and credit cards secured by deposit accounts, as well as unsecured credit cards and business loans.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, these other loans totaled $219,000, or 0.20% of the total loan portfolio.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Origination and Servicing of Loans.&#160;&#160;</font>Historically, the Association has originated mortgage loans pursuant to underwriting standards that generally conform with the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac guidelines.&#160;&#160;Loan origination activities are primarily concentrated in Brooklyn, as well as the other four boroughs of New York City, and Long Island, New York. Properties securing real estate and construction loans are primarily located in Brooklyn, Queens, Long Island and Manhattan.&#160;&#160;New loans are generated primarily from walk-in customers, customer referrals, a network of mortgage brokers, and other parties with whom the Association does business, and from the efforts of employees and advertising.&#160;&#160;Loan applications are underwritten and processed at the main office.&#160;&#160;The Association services all loans that it originates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loan Approval Procedures and Authority</font>.&#160;&#160;The loan approval process is intended to assess the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan, the viability of the loan, and the adequacy of the value of the property that will secure the loan.&#160;&#160;To assess the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay, the Association reviews the employment and credit history and information on the historical and projected income and expenses of mortgagors or if applicable, the historical and projected income and expenses of the property.&#160;&#160;All loans&#160;&#160;are approved by the board of directors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Association requires appraisals of all real property securing loans, and if applicable, environmental inspections.&#160;&#160;Appraisals are performed by independent licensed appraisers.&#160;&#160;All appraisers are approved by the board of directors. The Association requires fire and extended coverage insurance in amounts at least equal to the principal amount of the loan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Non-performing and Problem Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">After a mortgage loan becomes 10 days past due, a computer generated late notice is delivered to the borrower.&#160;&#160;A second late notice is sent once the loan becomes 16 days past due.&#160;&#160;When a loan becomes 30 days delinquent, a delinquency notice is sent to the borrower and an attempt is made to make personal contact with the borrower by letter or telephone from the head of the collection department to establish an acceptable repayment schedule.&#160;&#160;When a mortgage loan is 90 days delinquent and no acceptable resolution has been reached, the loan is placed in foreclosure and the property collateral is appraised and inspected.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Management is authorized to begin foreclosure proceedings on any loan after determining that it is prudent to do so.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Mortgage loans are reviewed on a regular basis and such loans, with the exception of loans guaranteed by the Federal Housing Administration, may be placed on non-accrual status when they become delinquent 90 days or more.&#160;&#160;When loans are placed on a non-accrual status, unpaid accrued interest is fully reserved, and further income is recognized only to the extent received. Loans guaranteed by the Federal Housing Administration may be placed on non-accrual status when they become delinquent 120 days or more.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Non-performing Loans.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>At December 31, 2010, $8.4 million, or 7.74%, of the Association&#8217;s total loans were non-performing loans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Non-performing Assets</font>.&#160;&#160;The table below sets forth the amounts and categories of the non-performing assets at the dates indicated.&#160;&#160;Delinquent loans that are 90 days or more past due are generally considered non-performing assets. There were no troubled debt restructurings during 2010 and one troubled debt restructuring of $400,000 during 2009.&#160;&#160;There were no restructured loans past due 90 days or more, or in a nonaccrual status at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, non-accruing loans consisted of eleven one-to four-family residential loans of $3.8 million with a corresponding $60,000 specific valuation allowance, four commercial real estate loans of $2.6 million with a corresponding $199,000 specific valuation allowance, two construction loan participations of $2.0 million with a corresponding $627,000 of specific valuation allowance and three credit card loans of $4,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Classified Assets.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>Office of Thrift Supervision regulations and the Association&#8217;s Asset Classification Policy provide that loans and other assets considered to be of lesser quality be classified as &#8220;substandard,&#8221; &#8220;doubtful&#8221; or &#8220;loss&#8221; assets.&#160;&#160;An asset is considered &#8220;substandard&#8221; if it is inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any. &#8220;Substandard&#8221; assets include those characterized by the &#8220;distinct possibility&#8221; that the institution will sustain &#8220;some loss&#8221; if the deficiencies are not corrected.&#160;&#160;Assets classified as &#8220;doubtful&#8221; have all of the weaknesses inherent in those classified &#8220;substandard,&#8221; with the added characteristic that the weaknesses present make &#8220;collection or liquidation in full,&#8221; on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, &#8220;highly questionable and improbable.&#8221; Assets classified as &#8220;loss&#8221; are those considered &#8220;uncollectible&#8221; and of such little value that their continuance as assets without the establishment of a specific loss reserve is not warranted.&#160;&#160;Management classifies an asset as &#8220;special mention&#8221; if the asset has a potential weakness that warrants management&#8217;s close attention.&#160;&#160;While such assets are not impaired, management has concluded that if the potential weakness in the asset is not addressed, the value of the asset may deteriorate, adversely affecting the repayment of the asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">An insured institution is required to establish general allowances for loan losses in an amount deemed prudent by management for loans classified substandard or doubtful, as well as for other problem loans.&#160;&#160;General allowances represent loss allowances which have been established to recognize the inherent losses associated with lending activities, but which, unlike specific allowances, have not been allocated to particular problem assets.&#160;&#160;When an insured institution classifies problem assets as &#8220;loss,&#8221; it is required either to establish a specific allowance for losses equal to 100% of the amount of the asset so classified or to charge off such amount.&#160;&#160;An institution&#8217;s determination as to the classification of its assets and the amount of its valuation allowances is subject to review by the Office of Thrift Supervision which can order the establishment of additional general or specific loss allowances.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On the basis of management&#8217;s review of its assets, at December 31, 2010 the Association had classified $3.8 million in one- to four-family residential loans, $3.2 million in commercial real estate loans, $2.0 million in construction loan participations and $4,000 in Visa credit card loans respectively, as substandard and $1.1 million in one to four family residential loans and $2.4 million in construction and land loan participations as special mention. The substandard construction loans of $2.0 million have specific valuation allowances of $627,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The loan portfolio is reviewed on a regular basis to determine whether any loans require classification in accordance with applicable regulations.&#160;&#160;Not all classified assets constitute non-performing assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Allowance for Loan Losses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Association&#8217;s allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level necessary to absorb loan losses which are both probable and reasonably estimable.&#160;&#160;Management, in determining the allowance for loan losses, considers the losses inherent in its loan portfolio and changes in the nature and volume of loan activities, along with the general economic and real estate market conditions.&#160;&#160;Management utilizes a two-tier approach: (1) identification of impaired loans and establishment of specific loss allowances on such loans; and (2) establishment of general valuation allowances on the remainder of the loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;Management maintains a loan review system, which allows for a periodic review of the loan portfolio and the early identification of potential impaired loans.&#160;&#160;Such system takes into consideration, among other things, delinquency status, size of loans, type and market value of collateral and financial condition of the borrowers.&#160;&#160;Specific loan loss allowances are established for identified losses based on a review of such information.&#160;&#160;A loan evaluated for impairment is considered to be impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Association will be unable to collect all amounts due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&#160;&#160;All loans identified as impaired are evaluated independently.&#160;&#160;Management does not aggregate such loans for evaluation purposes.&#160;&#160;Loan impairment is measured based on the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate or, as a practical expedient, at the loan&#8217;s observable market price or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.&#160;&#160;General loan loss allowances are based upon a combination of factors including, but not limited to, actual loan loss experience, composition of the loan portfolio, current economic conditions, management&#8217;s judgment and losses which are probable and reasonably estimable.&#160;&#160;The allowance is increased through provisions charged against current earnings and recoveries of previously charged-off loans.&#160;&#160;Loans which are determined to be uncollectible are charged against the allowance.&#160;&#160;While management uses available information to recognize probable and reasonably estimable loan losses, future loss provisions may be necessary based on changing economic conditions.&#160;&#160;The allowance for loan losses as of December 31, 2010 is maintained at a level that represents management&#8217;s best estimate of losses inherent in the loan portfolio, and such losses were both probable and reasonably estimable.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Payments received on impaired loans are applied to principal. The Association had twenty one loans totaling $9.0 million deemed to be impaired at December 31, 2010 and had three loans totaling $2.6 million deemed to be impaired at December 31, 2009. Impaired loans consisted of two construction loan participations of $2.0 million having $627,000 of specific valuation allowance, five commercial real estate loans of $3.2 million having $207,000 of specific allowances, eleven residential real estate loans of $3.8 million having specific allowances of $60,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#t">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Each quarter, management evaluates the total balance of the allowance for loan losses based on several factors that are not loan specific, but are reflective of the inherent losses in the loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;This process includes, but is not limited to, a periodic review of loan collectibility in light of historical experience, the nature and volume of loan activity, conditions that may affect the ability of the borrower to repay, underlying value of collateral, if applicable, and economic conditions in the Association&#8217;s immediate market area.&#160;&#160;First, loans are grouped by delinquency status.&#160;&#160;All loans 90 days or more delinquent are evaluated individually, based primarily on the value of the collateral securing the loan.&#160;&#160;Specific loss allowances are established as required by this analysis.&#160;&#160;All loans for which a specific loss allowance has not been assigned are segregated by type and delinquency status and a loss allowance is established by using loss experience data and management&#8217;s judgment concerning other matters it considers significant.&#160;&#160;The allowance is allocated to each category of loan based on the results of the above analysis.&#160;&#160;Small differences between the allocated balances and recorded allowances are reflected as unallocated to absorb losses resulting from the inherent imprecision involved in the loss analysis process.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This analysis process is inherently subjective, as it requires estimates that are susceptible to revisions as more information becomes available.&#160;&#160;Although management believes that it has established the allowance at levels to absorb probable and estimable losses, future additions may be necessary if economic or other conditions in the future differ from the current environment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Investments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Investments and Mortgage-Backed Securities</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>The Association&#8217;s investment portfolio at December 31, 2010 consisted of $808,000 in Federal Home Loan Bank of New York stock and $6.6 million in other interest-earning assets, consisting of deposits at other financial institutions and federal funds sold.&#160;&#160;The investment policy objectives are to maintain liquidity within the guidelines established by the board of directors. At December 31, 2010, the Association did not hold investments in any single entity (other than United States Government or agency sponsored entities) that had an aggregate book value in excess of 10% of its stockholder&#8217;s equity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sources of Funds</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General.&#160;&#160;</font>Deposits have traditionally been the primary source of funds for use in lending and investment activities.&#160;&#160;In addition to deposits, funds are derived from scheduled loan payments, investment maturities, loan prepayments and income on earning assets.&#160;&#160;While scheduled loan payments and income on earning assets are relatively stable sources of funds, deposit inflows and outflows can vary widely and are influenced by prevailing interest rates, market conditions and levels of competition.&#160;&#160;Borrowings from the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York may be used in the short-term to compensate for reductions in deposits and to fund loan growth.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Deposits.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>Deposits are not actively solicited outside of the New York City metropolitan area, and substantially all of the depositors are persons who work or reside in Brooklyn, New York.&#160;&#160;The Association offers a selection of deposit instruments, including demand deposits consisting of non-interest bearing and NOW accounts, passbook savings and club accounts, and fixed-term certificates of deposit.&#160;&#160;Deposit account terms vary, with the principal differences being the minimum balance required, the amount of time the funds must remain on deposit and the interest rate.&#160;&#160;The Association does not accept brokered deposits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest rates paid, maturity terms, service fees and withdrawal penalties are established on a periodic basis.&#160;&#160;Deposit rates and terms are based primarily on current operating strategies and market rates, liquidity requirements, rates paid by competitors and growth goals.&#160;&#160;Personalized customer service and long-standing relationships with customers are relied upon to attract and retain deposits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The flow of deposits is influenced significantly by general economic conditions, changes in money market and other prevailing interest rates and competition.&#160;&#160;The variety of deposit accounts offered allows the Association to be competitive in obtaining funds and responding to changes in consumer demand.&#160;&#160;Based on experience, management believes the deposits in the Association are relatively stable.&#160;&#160;However, the ability to attract and maintain certificates of deposit, and the rates paid on these deposits have been and will continue to be significantly affected by market conditions.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, $76.7 million, or 65.6% of deposit accounts were certificates of deposit, of which $61.7 million have maturities of one year or less.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Borrowings.</font>&#160;&#160;The Association may obtain advances from the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York upon the security of the common stock owned in the Federal Home Loan Bank and its qualifying residential mortgage loans and mortgage-backed securities, provided certain standards related to creditworthiness are met.&#160;&#160;These advances are made pursuant to several credit programs, each of which has its own interest rate and range of maturities.&#160;&#160;All borrowings consisted solely of fixed interest rate advances from Federal Home Loan Bank of New York.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the outstanding amount of these advances totaled $12.0 million. See Note 8 to the Consolidated Financial Statements included hereto in Exhibit 13.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Subsidiary Activities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Office of Thrift Supervision regulations permit federal savings associations to invest in the capital stock, obligations or other specified types of securities of subsidiaries (referred to as &#8220;service corporations&#8221;) and to make loans to such subsidiaries and joint ventures in which such subsidiaries are participants in an aggregate amount not exceeding 2% of the association&#8217;s assets, plus an additional 1% of assets if the amount over 2% is used for specified community or inner-city development purposes.&#160;&#160;In addition, federal regulations permit associations to make specified types of loans to such subsidiaries (other than special purpose finance subsidiaries) in which the association owns more than 10% of the stock, in an aggregate amount not exceeding 50% of the association&#8217;s regulatory capital if the association&#8217;s regulatory capital is in compliance with applicable regulations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Flatbush Federal has one active subsidiary, Flatbush REIT, Inc.&#160;&#160;Flatbush REIT, Inc. was incorporated in 2001 as a special purpose real estate investment trust under New York law.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Flatbush REIT, Inc. holds a portion of our mortgage related assets.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, Flatbush REIT, Inc. held $17.7 million in loans.</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">FEDERAL AND STATE TAXATION</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Federal Taxation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>Flatbush Federal Bancorp, Inc. and Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association are subject to federal income taxation in the same general manner as other corporations, with some exceptions discussed below.&#160;&#160;Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association&#8217;s tax returns have not been audited during the past five years.&#160;&#160;The following discussion of federal taxation is intended only to summarize certain pertinent federal income tax matters and is not a comprehensive description of the tax rules applicable to Flatbush Federal Bancorp, Inc. or Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Method of Accounting</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>For Federal income tax purposes, Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association currently reports its income and expenses on the accrual method of accounting and uses a tax year ending December 31 for filing its federal income tax returns.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Bad Debt Reserves</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>Prior to the Small Business Protection Act of 1996 (the &#8220;1996 Act&#8221;), Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association was permitted to establish a reserve for bad debts and to make annual additions to the reserve.&#160;&#160;These additions could, within specified formula limits, be deducted in arriving at our taxable income.&#160;&#160;Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association was required to use the specific charge off method in computing its bad debt deduction beginning with its 1996 federal tax return.&#160;&#160;Savings institutions were required to recapture any excess reserves over those established as of December 31, 1987 (base year reserve).&#160;&#160;Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association had approximately $3.4 million of pre-1988 bad debt reserves that are subject to recapture.&#160;&#160;During 2010, amendments of the New York State and New York City&#8217;s tax law and ordinance conformed the bad debt deduction to the deduction allowed under the Federal income tax law for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Taxable Distributions and Recapture</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>Prior to the 1996 Act, bad debt reserves created prior to January 1, 1988 were subject to recapture into taxable income if Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association failed to meet certain thrift asset and definitional tests.&#160;&#160;Federal legislation has eliminated these thrift related recapture rules.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2010, our total federal pre-1988 base year reserve was approximately $3.4 million.&#160;&#160;Under current law, pre-1988 base year reserves remain subject to recapture if Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association makes certain non-dividend distributions, repurchases any of its stock, pays dividends in excess of tax earnings and profits, or ceases to maintain a bank charter.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Alternative Minimum Tax</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>The Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;), imposes an alternative minimum tax (&#8220;AMT&#8221;) at a rate of 20% on a base of regular taxable income plus certain tax preferences (&#8220;alternative minimum taxable income&#8221; or &#8220;AMTI&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The AMT is payable to the extent such AMTI is in excess of an exemption amount and the AMT exceeds the regular income tax.&#160;&#160;Net operating losses can offset no more than 90% of AMTI.&#160;&#160;Certain payments of AMT may be used as credits against regular tax liabilities in future years.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association had $13,000 of AMT credits for carryover.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Net Operating Loss Carryovers</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>A financial institution may carry back net operating losses to the preceding two taxable years and forward to the succeeding 20 taxable years.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association had no net operating loss carry forwards for federal income tax purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Corporate Dividends-Received Deduction</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>Flatbush Federal Bancorp, Inc. may exclude from its income 100% of dividends received from Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association as a member of the same affiliated group of corporations.&#160;&#160;The corporate dividends-received deduction is 80% in the case of dividends received from corporations with which a corporate recipient does not file a consolidated return, and corporations which own less than 20% of the stock of a corporation distributing a dividend may deduct only 70% of dividends received or accrued on their behalf.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">State Taxation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">New York State Taxation</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>Flatbush Federal Bancorp, Inc. and Flatbush Federal Savings and Loan Association will report income on a calendar year basis to New York State.&#160;&#160;New York State franchise tax on corporations is imposed in an amount equal to the greater of (a) 7.1% of &#8220;entire net income&#8221; allocable to New York State, (b) 3% of &#8220;alternative entire net income&#8221; allocable to New York State, (c) 0.01% of the average value of assets allocable to New York State, or (d) nominal minimum tax.&#160;&#160;Entire net income is based on Federal taxable income, subject to certain modifications.&#160;&#160;Alternative entire net income is equal to entire net income without certain modifications.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Personnel</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2010, the Company had 34 full-time employees and two part-time employees.&#160;&#160;The employees are not represented by any collective bargaining group.&#160;&#160;Management believes that the Company has good relations with its employees.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SUPERVISION AND REGULATION</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Association is examined and supervised by the Office of Thrift Supervision and subject to the regulation of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC).&#160;&#160;This regulation and supervision establishes a comprehensive framework of activities in which an institution may engage and is intended primarily for the protection of the FDIC&#8217;s deposit insurance funds and depositors.&#160;&#160;Under this system of federal regulation, financial institutions are periodically examined to ensure that they satisfy applicable standards with respect to their capital adequacy, assets, management, earnings, liquidity and sensitivity to market interest rates.&#160;&#160;Following completion of its examination, the federal agency critiques the institution&#8217;s operations and assigns its rating (known as an institution&#8217;s CAMELS rating).&#160;&#160;Under federal law, an institution may not disclose its CAMELS rating to the public. The Association also is a member of and owns stock in the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York, which is one of the twelve regional banks in the Federal Home Loan Bank System.&#160;&#160;The Association also is regulated to a lesser extent by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, governing reserves to be maintained against deposits and other matters.&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision examines the Association and prepares reports for the consideration of its board of directors on any operating deficiencies.&#160;&#160;The Association&#8217;s relationship with its depositors and borrowers also is regulated to a great extent by both federal and state laws, especially in matters concerning the ownership of deposit accounts and the form and content of the Association&#8217;s mortgage documents.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the &#8220;Dodd-Frank Act&#8221;), signed by the President on July 21, 2011, provides for the regulation and supervision of federal savings institutions like the Association to be transferred from the Office of Thrift Supervision to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (&#8220;OCC&#8221;), the agency that regulates national banks.&#160;&#160;The OCC will assume primary responsibility for examining the Bank and implementing and enforcing many of the laws and regulations applicable to federal savings institutions.&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision will be eliminated.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The transfer will occur one year from July 21, 2010 enactment of the Dodd-Frank Act, subject to a possible six month extension.&#160;&#160;At the same time, the responsibility for supervising and regulating savings and loan holding companies will be transferred to the Federal Reserve Board, which currently supervises bank holding companies.&#160;&#160;The Dodd-Frank Act also provides for the creation of a new agency, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, as an independent bureau of the Federal Reserve Board, to take over the implementation of federal consumer financial protection and fair lending laws from the depository institution regulators.&#160;&#160;However, institutions of $10 billion or fewer in assets will continue to be examined for compliance with such laws and regulations by, and subject to the primary enforcement authority of, the prudential regulator rather than the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Certain regulatory requirements applicable to the Association, the Company and Flatbush MHC are referred to below or appear elsewhere in this Form 10-K. This regulatory discussion, however, does not purport to be an exhaustive treatment of applicable laws and regulations. Any change in these laws or regulations, whether by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Office of Thrift Supervision or Congress, could have a material adverse impact on the Association, the Company and Flatbush MHC operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Federal Banking Regulation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Business Activities.&#160;&#160;</font>A federal savings association derives its lending and investment powers from the Home Owners&#8217; Loan Act, as amended, and the regulations of the Office of Thrift Supervision.&#160;&#160;Under these laws and regulations, the Association may invest in mortgage loans secured by residential and commercial real estate, commercial business and consumer loans, certain types of debt securities and certain other assets.&#160;&#160;Certain types of lending, such as commercial and consumer loans, are subject to an aggregate limit calculated as a specified percentage of the Association&#8217;s capital or assets.&#160;&#160;The Association also may establish subsidiaries that may engage in activities not otherwise permissible for the Association, including real estate investment and securities and insurance brokerage.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Dodd-Frank Act authorizes, for the first time, the payment of interest on commercial checking accounts effective July 21, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Capital Requirements.</font>&#160;&#160;Office of Thrift Supervision regulations require savings associations to meet three minimum capital standards:&#160;&#160;a 1.5% tangible capital ratio, a 4% leverage ratio (3% for associations receiving the highest rating on the CAMELS rating system) and an 8% risk-based capital ratio.&#160;&#160;The prompt corrective action standards discussed below, in effect, establish a minimum 2% tangible capital standard.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The risk-based capital standard for savings associations requires the maintenance of Tier 1 (core) and total capital (which is defined as core capital and supplementary capital) to risk-weighted assets of at least 4% and 8%, respectively.&#160;&#160;In determining the amount of risk-weighted assets, all assets, including certain off-balance sheet assets, are multiplied by a risk-weight factor of 0% to 100%, assigned by the Office of Thrift Supervision based on the risks believed inherent in the type of asset.&#160;&#160;Core capital is defined as common stockholders&#8217; equity (including retained earnings), certain noncumulative perpetual preferred stock and related surplus and minority interests in equity accounts of consolidated subsidiaries, less intangibles other than certain mortgage servicing rights and credit card relationships.&#160;&#160;The components of supplementary capital currently include cumulative preferred stock, long-term perpetual preferred stock, mandatory convertible securities, subordinated debt and intermediate preferred stock, the allowance for loan and lease losses limited to a maximum of 1.25% of risk-weighted assets and up to 45% of net unrealized gains on available-for-sale equity securities with readily determinable fair market values.&#160;&#160;Overall, the amount of supplementary capital included as part of total capital cannot exceed 100% of core capital.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#t">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2010, the Association&#8217;s capital exceeded all applicable requirements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loans-to-One Borrower.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font> A federal savings association generally may not make a loan or extend credit to a single or related group of borrowers in excess of 15% of unimpaired capital and surplus.&#160;&#160;An additional amount may be loaned, equal to 10% of unimpaired capital and surplus, if the loan is secured by readily marketable collateral, which generally does not include real estate.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Association was in compliance with the loans-to-one borrower limitations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Qualified Thrift Lender Test.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>As a federal savings association, the Association is subject to a qualified thrift lender, or &#8220;QTL,&#8221; test.&#160;&#160;Under the QTL test, the Association must maintain at least 65% of its &#8220;portfolio assets&#8221; in &#8220;qualified thrift investments&#8221; in at least nine of the most recent 12 month period.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Portfolio assets&#8221; generally means total assets of a savings institution, less the sum of specified liquid assets up to 20% of total assets, goodwill and other intangible assets, and the value of property used in the conduct of the savings association&#8217;s business.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#8220;Qualified thrift investments&#8221; includes various types of loans made for residential and housing purposes, investments related to such purposes, including certain mortgage-backed and related securities, and loans for personal, family, household and certain other purposes up to a limit of 20% of portfolio assets.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Qualified thrift investments&#8221; also include 100% of an institution&#8217;s credit card loans, education loans and small business loans.&#160;&#160;The Association also may satisfy the QTL test by qualifying as a &#8220;domestic building and loan association&#8221; as defined in the Internal Revenue Code.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A savings association that fails the QTL test must operate under specified restrictions, including as to dividends.&#160;&#160;The Dodd-Frank Act makes noncompliance with the QTL test potentially subject to agency enforcement action for violation of law.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the Association maintained approximately 77.57% of its portfolio assets in qualified thrift investments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Capital Distributions.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Office of Thrift Supervision regulations govern capital distributions by a federal savings association, which include cash dividends, stock repurchases and other transactions charged to the capital account.&#160;&#160;A savings association must file an application for approval of a capital distribution if:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

</td>
